question: Can a TD-error-seeking exploration rule that detects and caps persistently high-TD-error transitions reach the sparse-reward goal faster than the plain TD-error-seeking rule in a small stochastic-reward gridworld?
method: Tabular Q-learning with error-seeking action selection on a simulated gridworld (sparse goal, noisy costly cells). Learning runs over agent seeds; main score is mean environment steps to first goal on held-out evaluation seeds. The improved cap quantile is chosen by leave-one-training-env-out CV on training seeds only.

dataset.name: Simulated stochastic-reward gridworld (generated in code)
dataset.source_url: none: generated in code, no download

metric_name: mean environment steps to first goal on held-out evaluation seeds (lower is better; capped at the step budget)
baseline: Tabular Q-learning; actions chosen by argmax of running mean |TD error| per state-action pair (stand-in for SEE's error-seeking objective), eps=0.05.
improved: Same agent, but each state-action pair keeps a TD-error history; pairs whose |TD error| stays high without decaying are flagged stuck and their exploration value is capped at a visited-value quantile (0, 0.25 or 0.5) chosen by leave-one-training-env-out CV. The earlier median-only cap left stuck pairs above well-explored goal-directed pairs, which is why it lost to the baseline.
notes: Simulated toy environment; tabular Q-learning, not SAC with neural networks, so this is only a stand-in for SEE. Only the improved variant's cap quantile was tuned, by CV on TRAIN_ENV; the baseline and the test seeds were not used for selection. The candidate grid includes the previous median cap, so the selected setting is no worse than it on training seeds. Steps are censored at the step budget. Only three agent seeds; no significance test. The stuck detector thresholds are design choices and results may not favour the improved variant.
